results.title: Itch.io alternatives? Just curious - Publishing - The Interactive Fiction Community Forum
results.content:
There are plenty of itch.io alternatives, although itch.io and IF Archive are the ones generally used by this community. You’ll notice older games on IFDB generally have IF Archive links, while newer ones tend to use Itch. But there’s also Newgrounds, where account creation is just as easy as Itch account creation, though Newgrounds only hosts web-compatible game and doesn’t allow downloaded files. [...] # Itch.io alternatives? Just curious

Hi all,

New member, just having a look around. One thing I noticed is a lot of the games seem to nearly always be hosted on itch.io, which got me wondering if there were any alternative places that writers publish their too?

It’s a bit like how it’s hard to think of an alternative to YouTube, but they do exist :laughing:

:laughing:

the best alternative, by far, remains the IF archive.

Best regards from Italy,  
dott. Piergiorgio.

Oh, I guess I’ve just not clicked enough stories on IF archive, because all the ones I tried had linked out to itch.io - but I get what you mean. [...] The IF Archive is the largest, and oldest repository of interactive fiction on the internet, but it’s not meant to be a “storefront” like itch.io. If you’re looking for a place to upload your game to, it’s a great choice, but nobody is likely to find it unless you also create an entry on the Interactive Fiction Database, or IFDB. The IFDB doesn’t host games, but it’s where the majority of IF fans go to find new ones and leave reviews. In terms of a like-for-like combination of “storefront” and “repository” for IF such as itch provides, there really isn’t one, and consequently most of the games listed on the IFDB are hosted either on itch, or on the Archive.

Edit: looks as though @lurker and I cross-posted. Their post goes into much more detail than mine.

results.title: Alternatives to Steam, Itch.io, and Gog ? - News & General Discussion - Unity Discussions
results.content:
# Alternatives to Steam, Itch.io, and Gog ?

Steam requires $100, Gog has a difficult acceptance process, and Itch.io seems to have a glut of free games which makes it difficult to gain many sales there (although I’ve seen some exceptions). Are there other alternatives?

Sounds like Steam and Gog have put in appropriate measures to solve the problem you see on Itch.io.

Publish a free “lite” version on Itch.io to get some marketing buzz. Publish your money-maker on Steam and/or Gog. But be warned, you’re going to need a lot more marketing than just a free sample on Itch.io. You need to be out there promoting your game on all sorts of places.

So basically you want an alternative platform to the only platforms where people actually buy games? [...] Game Jolt, PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo, iOS App Store, Android…

Of course each has pros and cons, and 3 of those have a far higher costs or much more onerous acceptance criteria than Steam or GoG.

Sounds like Steam and Gog have put in appropriate measures to solve the problem you see on Itch.io.

Pretty much. If that $100 fee wasn’t there then a lot of the stuff on itch would be on Steam instead or as well.

If you are worried your game won’t generate enough to cover the Steam fee, then just put it on itch.io. But keep in mind itch.io usually does not get anywhere near the sales that Steam gets.
